summary:
Ship Or Me? is a research-based app that helps tell whether a crew member's symptoms are likely caused by CO₂ levels in their surroundings or not.

Each astronaut does a short daily check-in, and a wearable records sleep and exercise. The app compares these readings with that astronaut's own normal. It also checks real ISS cabin data (from NASA's Open Science Data Repository) against NASA-STD-3001 limits. Then it answers one question: is it me, or the ship?
details:
How it works

- Each astronaut does a one-minute check-in: five 0–10 ratings plus symptoms. A simulated wearable fills in sleep and exercise.

- The app compares those answers with that person's own normal.

- It checks real ISS cabin telemetry (CO₂, temperature, humidity from NASA's Open Science Data Repository) against NASA-STD-3001 limits.

- If several crew drift at once while CO₂ is high, it says "likely the ship". If one person stays off after the air recovers, it says "likely you". If a personal problem lasts to day 3, it escalates to the flight surgeon on Earth.

Evidence (200 simulated crews over 10 real ISS cabin traces)

- On days with a CO₂ rise, 74% of alerts named the ship.

- 95% of one person's own problems were correctly not blamed on the ship.

- It opens 72% fewer personal cases than an app that raises one alert per person.

- The README also states the known blind spot: a personal problem that starts during a ship alert gets blamed on the ship until the air recovers.

What it is technically

- A static Vite + React + TypeScript app that you can install and use offline. There is no backend and no AI model in the product.

- It says "likely" and never diagnoses. It supports the flight surgeon rather than replacing one.

- The PIN login runs only in the browser. It's a privacy gate for the demo, not real security.

Repository link

Pages

- / is the login, with demo PINs: Anna 1111, Ben 2222, Chen 3333, Dana 4444 (medical officer), Mira 5555 (flight surgeon on Earth).

- /dashboard is each person's own dashboard on a 3D skeleton.

- /checkin is the daily check-in.

- /guide is plain-language explanations of each reading.

- /app is the medical console, for Dana and Mira only.

- /challenge is a public page with the evidence and a one-click judge's tour.

The app works offline with no server and no AI model. It never diagnoses. The same approach carries over to Antarctic winter stations, submarines and many more!

Tools

TypeScript, React, Vite and three.js for the web app. Python to download NASA data and run the tests on simulated crews, using the same rules as the app. Vitest for tests, deployed on Vercel. The app has no AI model. We used Claude Code as a coding assistant, and every AI contribution is logged in the repository.
